questions.question: In the month of September 2022, the Prime Minister Narendra Modi renamed Rajpath as _______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kartavya Path**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi officially renamed Rajpath as **Kartavya Path** on **September 8, 2022**.
 
• The renaming of Rajpath to Kartavya Path is part of a broader initiative to shed vestiges of colonialism.
 
• The term "Kartavya" means duty, emphasizing the importance of duty over power and authority.
 
• The renamed stretch runs from Rashtrapati Bhavan through India Gate to the National Stadium in New Delhi.
 
• This move reflects the government's aim to honor the values and duties upheld by the citizens and the administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajpath**

 
 
• Rajpath, originally known as Kingsway, is a ceremonial boulevard in New Delhi, India.
 
• It has historically been the site for the annual Republic Day parade on January 26th.
 
• The boulevard was designed by British architect Edwin Lutyens during the British colonial era.
 
 
 
• **Central Vista Project**
 
 
• The renaming of Rajpath is part of the larger Central Vista redevelopment project.
 
• This project aims to revamp the central administrative area of New Delhi, including the construction of a new Parliament building.
 
• The project is intended to symbolize a shift from colonial past to a future vision of modern India.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**
 
 
• Rajpath has been a key location for many significant national events and protests.
 
• It serves as a symbol of India's political power and central governance.
 
 
 
• **Public Reaction**
 
 
• The renaming has been met with mixed reactions, with some praising the move as a step towards decolonization.
 
• Critics argue that the renaming is symbolic and does not address more pressing governance issues.

questions.question: Which of the following is a global coalition launched in July 2020, created to make meaningful climate action faster and easier by independently tracking greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions with unprecedented detail and speed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Climate Trace**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Climate Trace is a global coalition launched in July 2020 to accelerate climate action by providing high-resolution data on greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• The initiative uses satellite imagery, remote sensing, and artificial intelligence to track emissions from sources worldwide with unprecedented detail and speed.
 
• Climate Trace aims to improve transparency and accountability in climate reporting and help nations meet their climate targets more effectively.
 
• It is supported by a diverse group of organizations, including technology companies, environmental NGOs, and research institutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Greenhouse Gases (GHGs)**

 
 
• GHGs are gases that trap heat in the atmosphere, contributing to the greenhouse effect and global warming.
 
• The primary GHGs include carbon dioxide (CO₂), methane (CH₄), nitrous oxide (N₂O), and fluorinated gases.
 
 
 
• **Satellite Imagery**
 
 
• Satellite imagery involves capturing images of Earth from space using satellites.
 
• This technology is crucial for monitoring environmental changes, natural disasters, and human activities.
 
 
 
• **Remote Sensing**
 
 
• Remote sensing is the acquisition of information about an object or phenomenon without making physical contact.
 
• It is widely used in environmental monitoring, agriculture, forestry, and urban planning.
 
 
 
• **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**
 
 
• AI refers to the simulation of human intelligence in machines programmed to think and learn.
 
• In climate monitoring, AI helps analyze large datasets, identify patterns, and predict future trends.

questions.question: Which of the following dances is performed by the Korku tribe?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chatkora**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chatkora** is a traditional dance form performed by the **Korku tribe**.
 
• The Korku tribe is primarily found in the Indian states of **Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra**.
 
• Chatkora dance is often performed during **festivals and community gatherings**, reflecting the cultural heritage of the tribe.
 
• This dance form is characterized by its **vibrant movements and rhythmic patterns**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Korku Tribe**

 
 
• The Korku tribe is an indigenous tribal community in India, recognized as one of the Scheduled Tribes.
 
• They primarily inhabit the regions of the Satpura range in Madhya Pradesh and parts of Maharashtra.
 
• Their traditional occupation includes farming, hunting, and gathering forest products.
 
• The Korkus have their own distinct language called "Korku," which belongs to the Munda language family.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Dances of Tribes in India**
 
 
• Tribal dances in India are an integral part of their culture and are performed during festivals, rituals, and social gatherings.
 
• These dances often convey stories, celebrate nature, and express communal harmony.
 
• Examples include the Santal dance by the Santal tribe and the War dance by the Nagas.
 
 
 
• **Preservation of Tribal Culture**
 
 
• The Indian government and various non-governmental organizations are actively working towards preserving the rich cultural heritage of tribal communities.
 
• Efforts include documentation, promoting traditional art forms, and providing platforms for showcasing their culture.
 
• Tribal museums and cultural festivals are organized to exhibit their traditions and crafts.

questions.question: Who was named as the Chairperson of the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT) in March 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chief Justice Dhirubhai Naranbhai Patel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chief Justice Dhirubhai Naranbhai Patel was appointed as the Chairperson of the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT) in March 2022.
 
• TDSAT was established to adjudicate disputes and hear appeals related to telecom, broadcasting, and information technology sectors.
 
• Prior to this appointment, D.N. Patel served as the Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court.
 
• The appointment of the chairperson is crucial for ensuring the smooth functioning of TDSAT in resolving sector-specific disputes.
 
• Chief Justice Patel's extensive experience in the judiciary is expected to contribute significantly to the tribunal's efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT)**

 
 
• Established in 2000, TDSAT adjudicates disputes and disposes of appeals related to the telecom, broadcasting, and IT sectors.
 
• The tribunal was set up under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997.
 
• It aims to ensure the protection of service providers and consumers' interests while promoting and ensuring the orderly growth of the telecom sector.
 
 
 
• **Role of TDSAT Chairperson**
 
 
• The chairperson heads the tribunal and oversees its functioning and administration.
 
• The chairperson is responsible for ensuring that disputes are resolved efficiently and fairly.
 
• The position requires significant legal expertise and experience in the judiciary to handle complex cases.
 
 
 
• **Qualifications for TDSAT Chairperson**
 
 
• The chairperson is usually a retired judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court.
 
• The appointment is made by the central government, considering the individual's experience and expertise in the legal field.
 
 
 
• **Importance of TDSAT**
 
 
• TDSAT plays a critical role in maintaining regulatory clarity and dispute resolution in the rapidly evolving telecom sector.
 
• It helps in fostering a competitive environment by ensuring that disputes are resolved promptly.

questions.question: How was the structure of the Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rectangle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro is one of the most famous structures found at the site of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• It is a large, rectangular tank located in the citadel area, which suggests its importance for ritualistic or ceremonial purposes.
 
• The tank measures approximately 12 meters long, 7 meters wide, and 2.4 meters deep.
 
• The structure is made of finely fitted bricks and features a series of steps leading down to the water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohenjo-daro**

 
 
• Mohenjo-daro is one of the largest settlements of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization, located in present-day Sindh, Pakistan.
 
• The name Mohenjo-daro means "Mound of the Dead" in Sindhi.
 
• The city was built around 2500 BCE and is known for its advanced urban planning and architecture.
 
 
 
• **Indus Valley Civilization**
 
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization was one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, contemporaneous with the civilizations of ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia.
 
• It flourished in the basins of the Indus River, which flows through present-day Pakistan and northwest India.
 
• The civilization is noted for its cities built of brick, roadside drainage systems, and multi-story houses.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Significance**
 
 
• The Great Bath is considered one of the earliest public water tanks in the ancient world.
 
• Its construction techniques, such as the use of bitumen for waterproofing, highlight the advanced engineering skills of the Indus Valley people.

questions.question: Expenditure made by the government for the creation of physical or financial assets is known as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Capital Expenditure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Capital Expenditure is the expenditure that is made by the government to create physical or financial assets.
 
• This may include the construction of roads, bridges, buildings, equipment, etc.
 
• The purpose of capital expenditure is to create long-term assets that will lead to economic growth in the future.
 
• This expenditure plays an important role in the government budget and is necessary to strengthen the economic structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue Expenditure**

 
 
• This is the expenditure incurred by the government for general administrative functions and services.
 
• It includes salaries, pensions, subsidies, and other administrative expenses.
 
• Revenue expenditure is intended to provide immediate services and not to create long-term assets.
 
 
 
• **Defence Expenditure**
 
 
• This expenditure is made for the maintenance and advancement of the military and defense services.
 
• It includes the salaries of soldiers, purchase of weapons, and expenses for military operations.
 
 
 
• **Subsidy Expenditure**
 
 
• This expenditure is made by the government to provide subsidies in various sectors, such as agriculture, food security, and fuel.
 
• Its purpose is to provide financial support to the poor and low-income groups.
 
 
 
• **Financial Assets**
 
 
• These are assets that are held by the government as investments, such as government bonds, stocks, etc.
 
• The purpose of financial assets is to provide financial stability and generate income from investments.

questions.question: Which of the following temples is NOT a 'Shakti Peeth'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Omkareshwar temple**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Omkareshwar temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is one of the twelve revered Jyotirlinga shrines of Shiva.
 
• It is located on Mandhata Island in the Narmada River in the state of Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• The temple represents one of the most significant pilgrimage destinations for followers of Hinduism focusing on Shiva worship.
 
• Unlike the other options listed, Omkareshwar is not classified as a Shakti Peeth, which are shrines and pilgrimage destinations dedicated to the goddess Shakti or Sati.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shakti Peeths**

 
 
• Shakti Peeths are significant shrines and pilgrimage destinations in Shaktism, the goddess-focused Hindu tradition.
 
• They are dedicated to the goddess Shakti, the divine feminine power, and are located throughout the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Each Shakti Peeth is associated with a body part of the goddess Sati, which is said to have fallen at that location.
 
• Famous Shakti Peeths include Kamakhya Temple in Assam, Kalighat Temple in West Bengal, and Kalmadhav Temple in Maharashtra.
 
 
 
• **Jyotirlinga**
 
 
• Jyotirlingas are shrines where Lord Shiva is worshipped in the form of a fiery column of light.
 
• There are twelve traditional Jyotirlinga shrines in India, considered highly sacred by Hindus.
 
• Omkareshwar is one of these twelve Jyotirlingas, representing the infinite nature of Shiva.
 
 
 
• **Kamakhya Temple**
 
 
• Located in Guwahati, Assam, it is one of the oldest and most revered Shakti Peeths in India.
 
• The temple is dedicated to the goddess Kamakhya, an incarnation of Sati.
 
 
 
• **Kalighat Temple**
 
 
• Situated in Kolkata, West Bengal, Kalighat is a famous Shakti Peeth dedicated to goddess Kali.
 
• The temple is one of the 51 Shakti Peeths and a major pilgrimage site.

questions.question: Mool Shanker was the early name of whom among the following social reformers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dayanand Saraswati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mool Shanker was the early name of **Dayanand Saraswati**.
 
• Dayanand Saraswati was a renowned Hindu religious leader and founder of the **Arya Samaj**.
 
• He was born on **12 February 1824** in Tankara, Gujarat.
 
• Dayanand Saraswati promoted the principles of the **Vedas** and condemned idol worship and social evils.
 
• He is well-known for his slogan "**Back to the Vedas**," urging a return to the ancient Vedic teachings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arya Samaj:**

 
 
• Founded by Dayanand Saraswati on 10 April 1875.
 
• Aims to promote values and practices based on the infallibility of the Vedas.
 
• Opposes caste system, child marriage, and gender discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Satyarth Prakash:**
 
 
• Major work of Dayanand Saraswati, also known as "The Light of Truth."
 
• A critical analysis of various religious beliefs and practices.
 
• Promotes rational thinking and Vedic ideology.
 
 
 
• **Shuddhi Movement:**
 
 
• Initiated by Dayanand Saraswati to reconvert those who had converted to other religions back to Hinduism.
 
• Emphasizes the purification of individuals and society.
 
• Aims to restore the Vedic religion and culture.
 
 
 
• **Education Reforms:**
 
 
• Dayanand Saraswati advocated for modern education, including science and technology, alongside Vedic teachings.
 
• Stressed on the importance of education for women and the underprivileged.
 
• Established several educational institutions promoting a blend of Vedic and modern education.

questions.question: The Fundamental Duties are encapsulated under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51 A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 51 A of the Indian Constitution deals with the Fundamental Duties of citizens.
 
• Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Originally, there were ten Fundamental Duties, but the 86th Amendment Act in 2002 added an eleventh duty.
 
• These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by law but serve as moral obligations for citizens.
 
• The Fundamental Duties encompass respect for the Constitution, national symbols, and institutions, promoting harmony, protecting the environment, and striving for excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swaran Singh Committee:**

 
 
• Established in 1976, the committee was headed by Sardar Swaran Singh, the then Minister of External Affairs.
 
• It was tasked with examining the Constitution and recommending changes to strengthen it, leading to the inclusion of Fundamental Duties.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act (1976):**
 
 
• Also known as the "Mini-Constitution," it brought extensive changes to the Constitution, including the addition of Fundamental Duties.
 
• It aimed to curb the abuse of power and reinforce the responsibility of citizens towards the nation.
 
 
 
• **86th Amendment Act (2002):**
 
 
• This amendment added the eleventh Fundamental Duty, which emphasizes the responsibility of parents or guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children between the ages of six and fourteen.
 
 
 
• **Non-justiciable Nature:**
 
 
• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by courts.
 
• They serve as moral guidelines for citizens to follow, promoting a sense of duty and discipline.
 
 
 
• **List of Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• Respect the Constitution, national flag, and national anthem.
 
• Uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• Promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood.
 
• Value and preserve the rich heritage of the country's composite culture.
 
• Protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife.

questions.question: Which of the following portals was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment to bring transparency and accountability to the enforcement of labour laws and ease compliance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shram Suvidha Portal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Shram Suvidha Portal** was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment to bring transparency and accountability in the enforcement of labour laws and ease compliance.
 
• The portal provides a single platform for **registration of establishments under various labour laws**.
 
• It aims to minimize the complexity and ensure **ease of doing business** by providing a unified online platform.
 
• Shram Suvidha Portal allows for the **filing of online returns** for compliance with 44 labour laws.
 
• The portal also generates a **Labour Identification Number (LIN)** for each establishment, ensuring a unique identity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PRAAPTI (Payment Ratification and Analysis in Power procurement for bringing Transparency in Invoicing of generators)**

 
 
• It is a web portal launched by the Ministry of Power to provide transparency in power purchase transactions between Generators and Discoms.
 
• The portal captures the invoicing and payment data for various long-term Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs).
 
• It helps stakeholders to monitor the outstanding payments and payment delays in the power sector.
 
 
 
• **Saubhagya (Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana)**
 
 
• Launched by the Government of India to ensure electrification of all willing households in the country.
 
• It aims to provide electricity connections to all remaining un-electrified households in rural as well as urban areas.
 
• The scheme targets to achieve universal household electrification in the country.
 
 
 
• **E-NAM (National Agriculture Market)**
 
 
• A pan-India electronic trading portal launched by the Ministry of Agriculture to create a unified national market for agricultural commodities.
 
• It facilitates farmers, traders, and buyers with online trading in commodities.
 
• The platform integrates Agricultural Produce Market Committees (APMCs) across the country.

questions.question: Which state has the highest sex ratio in India as per the 2011 Census?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the 2011 Census, Kerala has the highest sex ratio among Indian states, with 1084 females per 1000 males.
 
• The sex ratio is a critical demographic indicator representing the number of females per 1000 males in a population.
 
• Kerala has consistently maintained a high sex ratio due to better healthcare, higher literacy rates, and improved social status for women.
 
• The state has various social and welfare programs aimed at supporting and empowering women.
 
• Kerala’s high sex ratio is also a reflection of its progressive social policies and emphasis on gender equality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sex Ratio**

 
 
• Sex ratio is an important metric in demographics, indicating the balance between the number of males and females in a population.
 
• A balanced or higher sex ratio is often associated with better health and social indicators for women.
 
• Sex ratio can be influenced by factors such as gender-specific mortality rates, cultural practices, and migration patterns.
 
 
 
• **2011 Census**
 
 
• The Census of India 2011 is the 15th National Census since 1872.
 
• It provides comprehensive data on the demographic, economic, and social characteristics of the Indian population.
 
• The census collects data on various parameters including population size, sex ratio, literacy rates, and employment.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Sex Ratio**
 
 
• Healthcare: Access to healthcare services can reduce female mortality rates, positively impacting the sex ratio.
 
• Education: Higher literacy rates among women lead to greater awareness and improved social status.
 
• Social Policies: Government initiatives aimed at gender equality can improve the sex ratio.
 
 
 
• **Gender Equality in Kerala**
 
 
• Kerala’s achievements in gender equality are attributed to its high literacy rates and effective public health system.
 
• Women in Kerala have greater access to education and employment opportunities compared to many other Indian states.
 
• Kerala’s social reforms and progressive policies have played a significant role in empowering women and enhancing their social status.

questions.question: Select the correct pair of festival and its corresponding state from among the following.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Desert Festival: Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Desert Festival is an annual event that takes place in the city of **Jaisalmer, Rajasthan**.
 
• The festival is a three-day extravaganza held every year in **February**.
 
• It showcases the rich cultural heritage of Rajasthan through **folk music, dance, and traditional sports**.
 
• Major attractions include **camel races, turban tying competitions, and the Mr. Desert contest**.
 
• The event is organized by the **Rajasthan Tourism Department** to promote tourism in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajasthan's Cultural Significance**

 
 
• Rajasthan is known for its rich cultural history and heritage.
 
• The state hosts various festivals that highlight its traditions, including the Pushkar Fair and the Teej Festival.
 
 
 
• **Jaisalmer**
 
 
• Jaisalmer, also known as the "Golden City," is famous for its yellow sandstone architecture.
 
• The Jaisalmer Fort, one of the largest forts in the world, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Tourism in Rajasthan**
 
 
• Rajasthan is a popular tourist destination, known for its palaces, forts, and vibrant culture.
 
• It attracts millions of domestic and international tourists each year.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Festivals**
 
 
• Other notable festivals in Rajasthan include the Jaipur Literature Festival and the Marwar Festival.
 
• These festivals also contribute significantly to the cultural and economic landscape of the state.

questions.question: Researchers of which country first discovered the "Plastic eating Bacteria" in 2016?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Japan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 2016, researchers from Japan discovered a strain of bacteria capable of breaking down and consuming polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastic.
 
• The bacteria, named Ideonella sakaiensis, was found at a waste recycling center outside of Osaka.
 
• Ideonella sakaiensis uses two enzymes to hydrolyze PET into its monomers, which are then assimilated by the bacteria.
 
• This discovery offers potential solutions for addressing plastic pollution, a significant environmental concern globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET)**

 
 
• PET is a type of plastic commonly used in packaging, including bottles and containers.
 
• It is known for its strength, thermal stability, and transparency, making it widely used in the food and beverage industry.
 
• PET is non-biodegradable and poses significant environmental challenges due to its persistence in the environment.
 
 
 
• **Plastic Pollution**
 
 
• Plastic pollution refers to the accumulation of plastic objects and particles in the Earth's environment adversely affecting wildlife, wildlife habitat, and humans.
 
• It is a major environmental issue, with millions of tons of plastic waste entering the oceans each year.
 
• Efforts to mitigate plastic pollution include recycling, bioplastics, and reducing plastic use through policy measures.
 
 
 
• **Biodegradation**
 
 
• Biodegradation is the process by which organic substances are broken down by the actions of living organisms, typically microorganisms.
 
• This process is essential for the natural breakdown of waste products and is crucial in waste management and environmental cleanup.
 
 
 
• **Enzymatic Hydrolysis**
 
 
• Enzymatic hydrolysis is a process where enzymes break down complex molecules into simpler ones, often used in the degradation of plastics.
 
• In the context of PET degradation, specific enzymes break the ester bonds in the polymer to produce monomers that can be further metabolized by microorganisms.

questions.question: In which of the Five-Year Plans was 'The Twenty Point Programme' launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fifth Five-Year Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Twenty Point Programme was launched in India during the Fifth Five-Year Plan period (1974-79).
 
• It was introduced by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on 1st July 1975.
 
• The programme aimed at poverty eradication, employment generation, and improvement of quality of life.
 
• The focus was on areas like health, education, housing, and social welfare to uplift the marginalized sections of society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans in India**

 
 
• India's Five-Year Plans were centralized economic and social growth programs modeled after the Soviet Union's planning system.
 
• The first Five-Year Plan was launched in 1951, focusing on agriculture and infrastructure development.
 
• The plans aimed to achieve self-reliant and robust economic growth, reducing poverty, and improving living standards.
 
 
 
• **Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-79)**
 
 
• It aimed at economic self-reliance and poverty reduction, with a focus on employment generation.
 
• Major projects included the National Program for Minimum Needs and the Twenty Point Programme.
 
• The plan faced challenges due to the global oil crisis and inflationary pressures.
 
 
 
• **Indira Gandhi's Policies**
 
 
• Indira Gandhi, the then Prime Minister, introduced several socio-economic reforms in the 1970s.
 
• Her policies focused on poverty alleviation, land reforms, and increasing agricultural productivity.
 
• She nationalized banks in 1969 to ensure credit availability to the underprivileged.
 
 
 
• **Poverty Alleviation Programs**
 
 
• India has implemented various programs to alleviate poverty, such as the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA).
 
• These programs aim to provide employment, improve infrastructure, and support vulnerable populations.

questions.question: In 1911, air transport in India began between which two places?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Allahabad and Naini**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first commercial civil aviation flight in India took place on February 18, 1911.
 
• The flight was operated between Allahabad and Naini, covering a distance of approximately 6 miles.
 
• The aircraft used was a Humber biplane, piloted by French aviator Henri Piquet.
 
• This historic flight carried 6,500 letters, marking the beginning of airmail services in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Civil Aviation in India**

 
 
• India's first airstrip was built in the early 1920s in Karachi, which was then part of British India.
 
• The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is the regulatory body overseeing civil aviation in India.
 
• Air India, founded in 1932 by J.R.D. Tata, was the first Indian airline.
 
• India's aviation sector is one of the fastest-growing in the world, with numerous domestic and international carriers.
 
 
 
• **Henri Piquet**
 
 
• Henri Piquet was a pioneering French aviator known for his contributions to early aviation.
 
• He piloted the first airmail flight in India on February 18, 1911.
 
• His flight between Allahabad and Naini marked a significant milestone in the history of Indian aviation.
 
 
 
• **Airmail Services**
 
 
• The concept of airmail involves transporting mail via aircraft, significantly reducing delivery times.
 
• Airmail services have played a crucial role in connecting remote and inaccessible areas.
 
• Modern airmail services are integrated with logistics and courier companies, providing fast and reliable delivery solutions.
 
 
 
• **Humber Biplane**
 
 
• The Humber biplane was an early British aircraft designed and built by the Humber Motor Company.
 
• It was used in the first airmail flight in India, piloted by Henri Piquet.
 
• Biplanes have two main wings stacked one above the other, providing greater lift and stability.

questions.question: Which of the following newspapers in British India was founded by Bal Gangadhar Tilak?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kesari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kesari** was a Marathi-language newspaper founded by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in 1881.
 
• Tilak used Kesari as a platform to criticize the British rule in India and advocate for self-rule.
 
• The newspaper played a significant role in the Indian independence movement, spreading nationalist ideas and uniting people.
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak, also known as Lokmanya Tilak, was a prominent freedom fighter and social reformer.
 
• Kesari's incisive articles and editorials were instrumental in awakening political consciousness among Indians.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**

 
 
• He was one of the first and strongest advocates of Swaraj (self-rule) and is often referred to as the "Father of the Indian Unrest".
 
• Tilak was a founder member of the Indian National Congress and played a pivotal role in its early years.
 
• He was also a scholar, mathematician, and a writer, contributing significantly to Indian literature and education.
 
• His famous slogan, "Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it", became a rallying cry for Indian nationalists.
 
 
 
• **Role of Newspapers in the Indian Independence Movement**
 
 
• Newspapers like Kesari were crucial in spreading nationalist ideas and mobilizing public opinion against British colonial rule.
 
• They provided a platform for leaders to communicate their ideas and strategies to the masses.
 
• Other notable newspapers of the time included The Hindu, Amrita Bazar Patrika, and Swadesamitran.
 
• Through journalism, many leaders were able to circumvent British censorship and repression.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Kesari**
 
 
• Keshari helped in fostering a sense of unity and nationalism among the Indian population.
 
• It provided a voice to the common people and highlighted issues such as poverty, discrimination, and injustice.
 
• The newspaper also played a role in educating the masses about their rights and the importance of self-governance.
 
• Despite facing numerous bans and censorships, Kesari continued to influence and inspire generations of freedom fighters.

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: Tattvabodhini Sabha was founded in ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1839**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tattvabodhini Sabha was founded in 1839 in Calcutta (now Kolkata), India.
 
• The Sabha was established by Debendranath Tagore, father of the famous poet Rabindranath Tagore.
 
• Its main objective was to promote the religious and social ideas of the Brahmo Samaj.
 
• The Tattvabodhini Sabha played a significant role in the Bengal Renaissance by encouraging rational thinking and modern education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmo Samaj**

 
 
• Founded in 1828 by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, the Brahmo Samaj was a reform movement of Hinduism.
 
• It emphasized monotheism, rationalism, and modern education.
 
• The movement aimed to eliminate social evils like Sati and child marriage.
 
 
 
• **Bengal Renaissance**
 
 
• A period of social and cultural reform in Bengal during the 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
• Marked by a revival of interest in Indian culture, coupled with a strong influence of Western ideas.
 
• Key figures included Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, and Rabindranath Tagore.
 
 
 
• **Debendranath Tagore**
 
 
• One of the leading figures of the Brahmo Samaj after Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
 
• He founded the Tattvabodhini Sabha to propagate the teachings of the Brahmo Samaj.
 
• He was instrumental in the spread of Brahmoism in Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Social Reforms**
 
 
• The Tattvabodhini Sabha contributed to various social reforms, including education and women's rights.
 
• The Sabha's journal, Tattvabodhini Patrika, was a significant medium for spreading reformist ideas.

questions.question: Zainul Abidin was one of most famous rulers of which kingdom in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kashmir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Zainul Abidin, also known as Bud Shah, was the eighth Sultan of Kashmir, ruling from 1420 to 1470.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Akbar of Kashmir" for his policies of religious tolerance and efforts to promote cultural and economic prosperity.
 
• Under his rule, Kashmir saw significant developments in arts, crafts, music, and architecture.
 
• Zainul Abidin played a crucial role in reviving the economy of Kashmir by promoting silk weaving, carpet making, and shawl manufacturing.
 
• He is also credited with the introduction of new agricultural techniques and the fostering of trade relations with Central Asia and Persia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kashmir Sultanate:**

 
 
• The Kashmir Sultanate was established by Shams-ud-Din Shah Mir in 1339, marking the beginning of Muslim rule in the region.
 
• The Sultanate period saw the introduction of Persian culture and language in Kashmir.
 
• The region became a center of learning and culture, attracting scholars, poets, and artisans.
 
• The rule of the Kashmir Sultanate lasted until 1586, when it was annexed by the Mughal Empire.
 
 
 
• **Zainul Abidin's Reforms:**
 
 
• Zainul Abidin introduced land revenue reforms to improve agricultural productivity.
 
• He established a well-organized administrative system with efficient officials to maintain law and order.
 
• He promoted education by establishing schools and madrasas (Islamic educational institutions).
 
• He encouraged the translation of Sanskrit texts into Persian, fostering cultural integration.
 
 
 
• **Religious Tolerance:**
 
 
• Zainul Abidin is known for his policy of religious tolerance, allowing the free practice of different religions.
 
• He respected Hindu customs and festivals, and even participated in some Hindu rituals.
 
• He abolished the jizya (poll tax) on non-Muslims, promoting harmony among different communities.
 
• His court included both Hindu and Muslim scholars, reflecting his inclusive approach to governance.
 
 
 
• **Cultural and Economic Contributions:**
 
 
• Under Zainul Abidin's rule, Kashmir became renowned for its fine arts, including pottery, paper-mâché, and wood carving.
 
• He established trade relations with other regions, boosting the economy of Kashmir.
 
• He introduced new crops like grapes and fruits, contributing to agricultural diversity.
 
• His patronage of arts and crafts led to the flourishing of Kashmiri shawls and carpets, which gained international fame.

questions.question: Which hill is NOT a part of the Meghalaya Plateau from the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nilgiri Hills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Meghalaya Plateau, also known as the Shillong Plateau, is located in the northeastern part of India.
 
• It comprises three main hill ranges: the Garo Hills, the Khasi Hills, and the Jaintia Hills.
 
• Garo Hills are located in the western part of the Meghalaya state.
 
• Khasi Hills are situated in the central part of Meghalaya, while the Jaintia Hills lie to the east of the Khasi Hills.
 
• The Nilgiri Hills are located in the southern part of India, primarily in Tamil Nadu, and are not part of the Meghalaya Plateau.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Meghalaya Plateau**

 
 
• It is part of the larger Indian Peninsular Plateau and is known for its rich biodiversity and distinct climatic conditions.
 
• The plateau is a significant watershed area, giving rise to numerous rivers like the Brahmaputra and the Barak.
 
• Due to heavy rainfall, the region is covered with lush green vegetation, and it is one of the wettest places on Earth.
 
• The region is also famous for its living root bridges, a marvel of bioengineering made by local tribes.
 
 
 
• **Nilgiri Hills**
 
 
• The Nilgiri Hills are part of the Western Ghats, spanning Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Kerala.
 
• The highest peak in the Nilgiris is Doddabetta, standing at 2,637 meters above sea level.
 
• This region is known for its tea plantations, rich biodiversity, and pleasant climate, making it a popular tourist destination.
 
• The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, part of the hills, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and home to several endangered species.

questions.question: Which of the following incomes is NOT included in the factor income?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Scholarship of a student**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Factor income includes earnings from production factors like land, labor, and capital, which are rent, wages, and interest respectively.
 
• Scholarships are financial aids provided to students to support their education and do not arise from the production process.
 
• Factor income typically covers payments for the services of factors of production in the production of goods and services.
 
• Examples of factor income include rent (land), wages (labor), and interest (capital).
 
• Scholarships are considered transfer payments and are not included in the national income calculations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Factor Income**

 
 
• Factor income refers to the income derived from the factors of production: land, labor, and capital.
 
• This income includes wages, interest, rent, and profits.
 
• It is a key component in the calculation of national income and GDP.
 
 
 
• **Transfer Payments**
 
 
• Transfer payments are non-exchange transactions where no goods or services are exchanged.
 
• Examples include scholarships, social security benefits, and unemployment benefits.
 
• They are not included in national income as they do not reflect the production of goods and services.
 
 
 
• **National Income**
 
 
• National income is the total value of all goods and services produced by a country over a specific period, typically a year.
 
• It includes factor incomes earned by residents from the production of goods and services.
 
• It is an important indicator of the economic health of a country.
 
 
 
• **Components of GDP**
 
 
• Gross Domestic Product (GDP) includes consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports.
 
• Factor incomes are part of the income approach to calculating GDP.
 
• Transfer payments are excluded from GDP calculations as they do not represent production.
